name: Street Custom 'Mockingbird' Voice-Activated Trap Gun
description: A concealed firearm — typically a sawed-off shotgun or heavy-caliber pistol — connected to a voice-recognition trigger that fires when it detects a specific spoken phrase or voice pattern. The Mockingbird is hidden behind walls, under furniture, or inside containers, aimed at a kill zone, and programmed to fire when the target speaks a particular word or when a specific person's voice is detected. The voice recognition uses salvaged smart-home assistant hardware, which means it is affordable, widely available, and approximately 85% accurate — the 15% error rate means Mockingbirds occasionally fire at the wrong person, which their deployers consider an acceptable margin. The weapon represents the intersection of cheap AI hardware and lethal intent.
specifications:
firearm: Variable — sawed-off shotgun, heavy pistol, or similar
trigger: Salvaged voice-recognition hardware
activation: Specific phrase or voice-pattern match
accuracy of recognition: approximately 85%
range: Determined by firearm and placement
power source: Battery-powered voice module, 72-hour standby
installation time: 30-60 minutes
concealment: Behind walls, under furniture, inside containers
story_hooks: A prominent community leader was killed when they said their own name at their front door — a Mockingbird had been installed inside their wall, programmed to their voice pattern.
Mockingbird traps programmed to common greetings have been found in abandoned buildings in Tier 1 — they are not targeted at anyone specific, they are designed to kill whoever enters.
related_entities: Carrion Defense Works Autonomous Perimeter Defense Ecosystem

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately fragmented assembly: a truncated shotgun or heavy pistol barrel emerging from jury-rigged polymer housing, festooned with exposed wiring and salvaged smart-home components. The overall impression is deliberately crude—parts that don't belong together welded into lethal intent. When concealed, only the muzzle or trigger mechanism protrudes from its hiding place.
physical_description.dimensions: Firearm body: 20-35cm (depending on base gun); voice module housing: 12-18cm × 8-12cm × 6-10cm; barrel protrusion: variable
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively heavy for its size—the salvaged voice hardware and ammunition load create unexpected heft. Feels crude and unbalanced when held; designed for mounting, not carrying.
physical_description.primary_material: Sawed-off steel/polymer firearm body; voice module encased in recycled smart-home plastic (often translucent or cracked); exposed copper and silver wiring; occasional rubber dampening mounts
physical_description.finish: Battle-scarred matte black on barrel; yellowed or cloudy plastic housing on voice module showing finger smudges and dust accumulation; exposed solder joints with oxidized copper patina; scratched mounting brackets
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: charcoal matte black (firearm), industrial gray (housing); Accents: tarnished copper wiring, occasional neon-green LED status indicator blinking in the plastic casing
physical_description.grip_texture: Not designed for gripping—firearm portion retains original grip (bare metal or worn rubberized); voice module mounting points are sharp-edged and unfinished, suited only for bolting into place
distinctive_features: Exposed voice-recognition microphone array visible through semi-translucent plastic
Single blinking LED (green for armed, red for triggered) set into the housing
Crimped battery connector visible with fraying insulation
Handwritten frequency calibration notes on housing in permanent marker
Jury-rigged heat vents—drilled holes in irregular patterns
Barrel crowned with a crude suppressor sleeve (often copper-stained)
Salvaged smart-home branding still faintly visible under the weapon housing
Custom voice-trigger test label taped to the side (e.g., 'PHRASE: ΦΦΦ trigger', partially peeling)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Original firearm manufacturer stamp on barrel (often filed or obscured); salvaged voice-module chip maker logo visible on circuit board through translucent housing; crude hand-stamped serial code on mounting bracket (usually 6-8 characters, inconsistent pressure creating uneven marks)
physical_description.condition_typical: Perpetually jury-rigged. Surface oxidation on exposed metal; dust and small debris lodged in wiring gaps; housing cracked or warped from heat cycling; tape repairs on non-critical components; the weapon looks perpetually on the verge of catastrophic failure, yet remains functional—a trait that makes it terrifying.
